text:
Alex: Quick sync — we're picking an internal API shape for routing/quotas before the console rollout. High level choices: proto-first gRPC service + HTTP/JSON gateway vs REST-first JSON endpoints. Thoughts?
Maria: Proto-first seems easier for typed routing/telemetry. We can embed route metadata in proto options and use generated headers.
Sam: Agree on typing, but ops cares about simpler HTTP for tracing/ingest pipelines. Quota enforcement sits at gateway — we need consistent header shape.
Rachel: Concern: browser clients can't call gRPC easily. Our SDKs would hide that but rollout UX matters. Can we do gRPC internally and a thin JSON shim at edge?
Jin: Thin shim + proto core = nice. But we lose field-level route claims unless shim translates faithfully. Need example header mapping.
Alex: Proposal: gRPC internal, envoy HTTP JSON gateway that translates. Headers: x-rw-route=<service/method>, x-rw-tenant, x-rw-quota-tags. Example:
```
# envoy config snippet
http_filters:
- name: envoy.filters.http.router
route_config:
  request_headers_to_add:
  - header:
      key: x-rw-route
      value: "%REQ(:path)%"
```
Maria: That mapping works. Add proto option: @route_metadata("quota_key") so generator can populate header automatically.
Sam: Telemetry: ensure gateway emits proto.method and proto.service as labels in metrics. That keeps dashboards consistent whether request came JSON or gRPC.
Rachel: For rollout UX: start with internal teams behind a feature flag. Console should show both "proto route" and "edge route" in one view.
Jin: Quotas: enforce at gateway with a consistent key, but downstream services should validate to avoid bypass. Dual-check until rollout completes.
Alex: Action items: Maria to draft proto options RFC, Sam to sketch Envoy translation docs, Rachel to mock console migration view. Ping @deploy-bot when ready for canary.
deploy-bot: noted: will schedule canary deploy once PRs are tagged. :robot_face:
Maria: I'll drop initial RFC by EOD and link here. Thanks all.
